request.spec:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export claims (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-claims"`) next to the people export. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the new export test and the three other scenarios in the spec.

**What the file contains:**
- The header line `person,number,date,amount,due,status,period`, then one line per claim.
- People come in list order, and every person is included, retired or not, whether or not "show retired" is on. Within each person, claims run oldest first. The screen lists them newest first, so the export reverses that order.
- The figures are the same as the claim row shows: the number (empty while a claim is a draft), the date, the amount, the due including any late charge, floor, statement or settled figure (`n/a` stays as it is), the status, and the period (empty when none).
- Quoting and line ends work like the people export: a field is wrapped in quotes only when it holds a comma, quote or line break (so `"Lee, Jo"`), and every line ends with a line feed. The file is named `claims-<sheet>.csv`.

**Where:** all the changes are in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. The due and period use the same calculations as the on-screen claim rows, so the export can't drift from what the screen shows. I also moved the download code out of `exportCsv()` into a small shared `download()` helper; the people export produces the same file as before.

No server or database changes were needed: the screen already has every value the export uses, and the export writes nothing to the audit file.
